cards.text: Malaysia's fire department counted 2,001 factory fires and RM4.21 billion lost, then pledged to strengthen enforcement
cards.sub: Its own figures show 2025 was the worst of those years: 463 factory fires, up 28.6 per cent, against a record 1,191 hazard notices issued.
sources: Bernama (BM), 31 Jul 2026, '2,001 Kes Kebakaran Kilang Dengan Kerugian RM4.21 Bilion Direkodkan Sejak Enam Tahun Lepas' - https://www.bernama.com/bm/jenayah_mahkamah/news.php?id=2588754

Malay Mail, 31 Jul 2026, 'Malaysia records 2,001 factory fires, RM4.21b losses since 2020, says Fire Dept D-G' - https://www.malaymail.com/news/malaysia/2026/07/31/malaysia-records-2001-factory-fires-rm421b-losses-since-2020-says-fire-dept-d-g/229793

Sinar Harian, 31 Jul 2026, '2,001 kes kebakaran kilang, kerugian cecah RM4.21 bilion sejak 2021 - JBPM' - https://www.sinarharian.com.my/article/790230/berita/semasa/2001-kes-kebakaran-kilang-kerugian-cecah-rm421-bilion-sejak-2021---jbpm

cards.h: JBPM inspected more factories in 2025 than in 2024 and issued 68.6 per cent more hazard notices. Fires rose too
cards.s: Inspections went from 1,563 to 1,878. Fire Hazard Elimination Notices went from 706 to 1,191. Factory fires hit 463, the highest of the six years reported.
cards.d: The Fire and Rescue Department's director-general, Datuk Seri Nor Hisham Mohammad, released both series in Putrajaya on 31 July 2026. Enforcement activity and fire incidence moved in the same direction in 2025: a 20.2 per cent rise in premises inspected, a 68.6 per cent rise in notices issued, and a 28.6 per cent rise in factory fires to 463 cases. The department has not offered a causal account of the 2025 peak, and none should be inferred from two series moving together. What the pairing does establish is that a year of unprecedented enforcement output was also the worst year on the record JBPM published.

cards.h: Factory fires were 2.9 per cent of Malaysia's fires in 2025 and 36.9 per cent of the money lost
cards.s: JBPM recorded 16,111 fires nationally that year, costing RM2.09 billion. Factories accounted for 463 of those cases and RM770.69 million of the losses.
cards.d: Both figures are the department's own and cover the same calendar year. The national total was given by deputy director-general (operations) Datuk Ahmad Izram Osman on 20 January 2026: 16,111 fires, RM2.09 billion in losses, 98 deaths, and RM6.44 billion in property saved. The factory subset, 463 cases and RM770.69 million, was reported on 31 July 2026. Dividing one into the other gives 2.9 per cent of cases and 36.9 per cent of losses. Fewer than three factory fires in every hundred fires, and better than a third of the national loss. The concentration is the point: this is where the money burns.
sources: Bernama (BM), 20 Jan 2026, '16,111 Kes Kebakaran Direkod Sepanjang 2025, Kerugian Cecah RM2.09 Bilion' - https://bernama.com/bm/news.php?id=2514748

cards.h: Since 1 January 2026 the annual fire-safety check on a factory can be signed by an officer the factory employs
cards.s: Section 28 of the Fire Services Act 1988 requires a fire certificate, renewable annually. JBPM now accepts an accredited in-house officer's report in place of its own yearly inspection, auditing every two to three years.
cards.d: Nor Hisham announced the change on 4 August 2025 at the Southern Zone Industry Lead Body Seminar, with effect from 1 January 2026. Accredited fire safety managers or officers conduct the internal testing and file the technical report for certificate renewal; JBPM retains an audit cycle of two to three years and can revoke accreditation and impose fines. More than 600 people had registered for training with HRD Corp and the Department of Skills Development. The statutory duty is unchanged: section 28 requires the annual certificate, and section 33 makes operating designated premises without one an offence carrying a fine up to RM50,000, up to five years' imprisonment, or both. What moved is the attestation, from the department to the premises. The regime is seven months old and the first half of 2026 recorded 222 factory fires.
sources: Fire Services Act 1988 (Act 341), AGC Laws of Malaysia clean draft 7 Mar 2019, ss.28, 33 - https://lom.agc.gov.my/act-detail.php?language=BI&act=341
Bernama, 4 Aug 2025, 'Accredited Fire Safety Officers To Be Granted Full Authority To Conduct Inspections' - https://bernama.com/en/news.php?id=2453029

cards.text: The question is not whether factories get inspected every year. It is who signs the inspection.
A restaurant that grades its own hygiene and hangs the certificate in the window, with the inspector due back sometime in the next three years.
sources: Bernama, 4 Aug 2025 (accredited officer files the renewal report; JBPM audits every two to three years) - https://bernama.com/en/news.php?id=2453029

cards.text: JBPM published every number here, including the ones that flatter it least, and a department short of inspectors has to ration them somehow. But a regime that reports more notices every year and more fires every year is measuring its own activity, not its effect. The 2026 figures will be the first written under self-attestation, and they are the ones worth waiting for.

sources: Bernama (BM) 31 Jul 2026; Bernama (BM) 20 Jan 2026; Bernama (EN) 4 Aug 2025; Fire Services Act 1988 (Act 341) AGC reprint clean draft 7 Mar 2019; Malay Mail 31 Jul 2026; Sinar Harian 31 Jul 2026
confidence: Medium-High - The 2025 and 2026-H1 case, loss and enforcement figures come from the state news agency reporting the department's own director-general, and the statutory text was read verbatim from the AGC reprint. Confidence is held below High for three reasons: the 463 / 28.6% / RM770.69m series for 2025 is single-sourced to Sinar Harian; the Fire Services (Amendment) Act 2025 gazette text was not opened, so the accreditation mechanism rests on Bernama reporting a spoken announcement; and the six-year window's start year is reported inconsistently across outlets, so no start year is stated anywhere in these cards.
needs_verification: The 1 January 2026 commencement date and the exact mechanism of the accredited-officer regime. Sourced to Bernama reporting the JBPM director-general on 4 Aug 2025, five months before commencement. The Fire Services (Amendment) Act 2025 (Act A1764) PDF on bomba.gov.my returned 503 and a direct fetch was reset. Stage 3 must open the gazette and confirm: commencement date, what the accredited officer certifies, what JBPM retains, and the audit interval. If the gazette contradicts the Bernama account, the Legal fact card and the analogy card both fall.

That factories are 'designated premises' under s.27 of Act 341, and therefore that the s.28 annual certificate duty applies to them. The designation order was not located. Every secondary description of the scope traces to fire-safety consultancy marketing pages, which were excluded as non-sources. The Legal fact card's framing depends on this.

The 2025 factory series: 463 cases, +28.6 per cent, RM770.69 million. Single-sourced to Sinar Harian. Every other outlet reported only the six-year lump. This is the base of the denominator claim in fact card 2 and of the peak claim in the hook.

That 'kilang' (factory, 463 cases in 2025) is a subset of 'industri' (industrial, 9.2 per cent of 12,292 structural fires, roughly 1,131 cases in 2025). Almost certainly true but unverified. No card mixes the two series, and the 2.9/36.9 per cent denominator compares factory cases against the all-fires total, which does not depend on this. Flagged so Stage 3 does not introduce the mixture while editing.

The start year of the six-year window. Malay Mail says 2020, Sinar Harian says 2021, Bernama says only 'the past six years'. No card states a start year. If Stage 3 resolves it against JBPM's annual statistics series, the hook may gain a year; until then it must not.
source_notes: Five discrepancies were handled rather than resolved silently. (1) Start year: three outlets reporting the same spoken statement give 2020, 2021, and no year. None is more authoritative than the others, so no card states a start year. (2) Case count: Bernama and Malay Mail give 2,001; Harian Metro's headline gives 2,002. The cards use 2,001, the state-wire figure carried by the majority. (3) The 2024 factory case count is nowhere reported. Dividing 463 by 1.286 implies roughly 360, but no source states it, so no card uses a 2024 case figure. The 2024 enforcement figures, 1,563 inspections and 706 notices, are reported directly and are used. (4) Category mismatch between 'factory' and 'industrial' is documented above and avoided in the copy. (5) RM4.21 billion over six years averages roughly RM702 million a year while 2025 alone was RM770.69 million, above that average. Because only two years are separately known, no card characterises the loss curve as flat, rising or falling. Two further notes on posture. The correlation between the 1 January 2026 accreditation switch and factory fire counts is not asserted as causal anywhere, and cannot be: the switch post-dates the 2025 peak. The view card states plainly that the 2026 figures are the first test. Unpublished T4A draft 1769 covers adjacent ground (58 per cent commercial-building fire-safety compliance) but has no brief or pipeline artifacts, and a previous T4A issue is not a primary source, so nothing from it was used.
